claim: Avoca AI is estimated at roughly $1,000-$3,500/month, cited to https://www.softwareadvice.com/product/651996-Avoca-AI/
problem: The cited page returned HTTP 403 and search summaries of it show no price (no reviews, no pricing published). The $1,000-$3,500 band in fact traces to ServiceAgent, a competitor selling AI answering to trades, which gives '$1,000-$3,000 mid-market, $2,500-$3,500 enterprise, billing per-minute' as its own unsourced estimate (documented on getmacha.com, which checked avoca.ai/pricing and got a 404 on 2026-09-24). The brief presents this figure twice (Avoca entry and buyer_reported_costs) with the wrong source and without saying the originating estimate came from a competitor and is unsourced.
fix: Replace the Software Advice citation with https://www.getmacha.com/blog/avoca-ai-pricing-explained (which itself attributes the number to serviceagent.ai) and label the figure 'competitor estimate, unsourced, Avoca publishes no price (avoca.ai/pricing 404 as of 24 Sep 2026)'. Consider dropping it from the full_service band, or widening that band to $700-$3,500 so it is carried by Hatch's operator-reported $700-$1,500 rather than by the unverifiable Avoca number.

claim: Jobber: 'no AI answering price published' (integrations_included), source https://api.settlejob.com/jobber-pricing/
problem: Contradicted by the cited page. It lists an AI Receptionist add-on at $29 a month sold separately and included in the Plus plan, plus Marketing Suite $99/mo and Pipeline $49/mo.
fix: Change Jobber integrations_included to: 'AI Receptionist add-on $29/month (also bundled in Plus); Marketing Suite $99/mo; Pipeline $49/mo — per settlejob.com, which quotes Jobber's pricing page (checked 4 Nov 2026); official Jobber page returned 403 to this tool'.

claim: 'the only published setup fee found in this segment is $299 one-time at Trueline IT' and Rilla setup_fee = 'Not public'
problem: Contradicted by the brief's own Rilla source: salesask.com reports a one-time setup fee of $1,500-$5,000 on top of $199-$349/rep/month. The Rilla entry repeats the per-rep price and the five-seat minimum from that page but omits the setup fee, which then makes the 'only setup fee' claim false.
fix: Add to Rilla setup_fee: '$1,500-$5,000 one-time, buyer-reported (salesask.com, updated 24 Oct 2026; Rilla publishes no price list)'. Reword the implication to 'the only vendor-published setup fee found is $299 at Trueline IT; the only other setup figure found is a buyer-reported $1,500-$5,000 at Rilla'.

claim: mid_market = '$299-$810/month for a trades-focused AI CSR or a hybrid human/AI desk with 500-1,000 minutes'
problem: The price span follows from the sourced tiers, but the '500-1,000 minutes' qualifier does not. The $810 anchor (Smith.ai human-first Basic) buys 90 calls, not 500-1,000 minutes; Abby $329-$599 buys 100-200 Abby Minutes, also well under 500. As written the label misdescribes what the top and bottom of the band include.
fix: Restate as '$299-$810/month for a trades-focused AI CSR or hybrid human/AI desk, ranging from 100-200 Abby Minutes (Abby $329-$599) or 90 calls (Smith.ai Basic $810) to 500-1,000 AI minutes (Sameday $449/$789, Goodcall Scale $299 at 2,000 unique customers)'. Keep the inference label.

claim: Smith.ai human-first tiers ($300/30 calls, $810/90, $2,100/300, overages $11.50/$10.50/$8.50), per-call add-on fees ($1.50 booking, $0.50 extra CRM, $0.50 SMS/Teams, $0.25 recording, $1.00 Spanish line), 'No setup fees' and the 30-day money-back guarantee are cited to https://smith.ai/pricing/ai-receptionist
problem: The AI-first pricing page shows none of these. All of them appear on the separate human-first page https://smith.ai/pricing/receptionists. The figures are correct for the vendor, but the citation points at a page that does not support them, and the add-on per-call fees belong to the human-first plan structure, not the AI-first tiers.
fix: Split the source_url: keep https://smith.ai/pricing/ai-receptionist for the Free/Pro/Enterprise AI tiers, and cite https://smith.ai/pricing/receptionists for the human-first tiers, the per-call add-on schedule, 'No setup fees' and the 30-day money-back guarantee (confirmed there: refund of plan and add-ons up to $1,000, overage excluded).

claim: ServiceTitan FSM tiers 'Starter / Essentials / The Works ... per-technician' and '$250-$500 per technician per month'
problem: Two problems. (a) The cited ServiceTitan podcast page covers only the AI Virtual Agent ($2.75/call) and says nothing about Starter/Essentials/The Works or per-technician FSM pricing. (b) CostBench, the source for the FSM figure, states the unit as per user/month (Starter $250, Essentials $398, The Works $498) and flags the prices 'unverified — last checked Jul 11, 2026'; it also reports a median contract of $1,500/year from 19 deals, which is inconsistent with $250-$498/user/mo. 'Per technician' is a unit change the source does not make.
fix: Cite costbench.com for the FSM tiers and write the unit as '$250-$498 per user/month, third-party, unverified (CostBench, checked 11 Jul 2026)'. Note CostBench's own median-contract figure conflicts with its list prices, so do not treat the FSM number as reliable. Remove the Starter/Essentials/The Works detail from the ServiceTitan podcast citation or re-source it.

claim: 'Every consumer-grade vendor advertises no setup fee (Goodcall, Rosie, Frontdesk, Abby, Smith.ai, SIAS)'
problem: Only Abby ('No Setup Fee'), Smith.ai ('No setup fees') and SIAS ('no setup fee') state it on their pages. Goodcall, Rosie and Frontdesk pages say nothing about setup fees at all — the brief's own tier fields correctly say 'None stated' for those three, so the implication overstates what they advertise.
fix: Reword to 'Abby, Smith.ai and SIAS explicitly advertise no setup fee; Goodcall, Rosie and Frontdesk publish no setup fee either way (none stated)'. Keep the $299 Trueline counterpoint.

claim: 'answering products run $299-$789/mo — roughly 5-10x the FSM subscription' (Housecall Pro $59/mo annual, Jobber Core $29-$49/mo)
problem: Inference arithmetic contradicts its own inputs: $299/$59 is about 5x, but $789/$59 is about 13x, and against Jobber Core at $29-$49 the multiple is roughly 6-27x. '5-10x' understates the top of the range it is describing.
fix: Restate as 'roughly 5-13x Housecall Pro's $59/mo entry plan and 6-27x Jobber Core at $29-$49/mo' (still labelled inference, and noting it compares a mid-band answering price to an entry-tier FSM plan).

claim: Avoca: 'Third-party listings describe a flat monthly fee based on conversation volume and CRM integration tier, with no per-seat fees'
problem: No opened source says this. The getmacha analysis found the only published estimates describe per-minute billing (from a competitor) and that 'billing unit: not published by Avoca'; avoca.ai's own construction web-chat page shows no pricing at all. 'Flat monthly fee based on conversation volume' is not attributable.
fix: Replace with 'Billing unit and price not published; avoca.ai/pricing returns 404 (checked 24 Sep 2026). The only circulating figures are a competitor's unsourced per-minute estimates ($1,000-$3,000 mid-market, $2,500-$3,500 enterprise).'

claim: Hatch Enterprise includes 'deeper data/API work scoped in Enterprise'
problem: The Hatch pricing page describes Enterprise as 'rich analytics and operational oversight' for multiple locations/divisions/service areas and lists 'account management and custom solutions' for every plan. It does not tie API/data work to Enterprise.
fix: Change to 'Enterprise adds analytics and multi-location/division oversight; 'custom solutions' are listed for all plans, not Enterprise only'.

claim: buyer_reported_costs Reddit figures ($200-$250/month weekday answering; $99/month after-hours up to 100 calls, ~$300/month 24/7, $400/week, year 2024) and the Reddit complaint set
problem: Both Reddit URLs could not be opened by this tool (readable extraction failed), so the numbers and the year '2024' are unverifiable from the source. This is not a failure by itself — the brief already caveats it — but the specific '2024' year and the dollar figures rest on search-result summaries only.
fix: Keep the caveat but mark the year as 'not verified' rather than '2024', and mark these entries 'unverified — search summary only' so nothing downstream treats the $300/month 24/7 figure as a sourced cost.
